extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (educational institutions), school administrators, HR and legal counsel responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Explanation and final-regulation requirements implementing Title IX protections for pregnancy, related conditions, lactation, voluntary leave, and pre-employment inquiries for recipient employees and students (including student-employees). Provides standards, interactions with other federal laws, and implementation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on employment discrimination based on pregnancy (§106.57(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not discriminate against employees based on current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions; regulatory text changed 'shall' to 'must' and removed the words 'or exclude from employment'. The Department interprets 'discriminate' to encompass exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to address barriers to professional achievement and ensure equal career opportunities; change in wording is for clarity and not to reduce coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions for employees (§106.57(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must treat an employee's pregnancy or related conditions as it does any other temporary medical condition for all job-related purposes, including commencement, duration and extensions of leave, payment of disability income, accrual of seniority, reinstatement, and under any fringe benefit offered to employees by virtue of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory language was revised to replace references to 'temporary disability' with 'temporary medical conditions' to avoid implying pregnancy is a disability. This provision is intended to be broad and standalone in effecting nondiscrimination for employees, but it does not obviate other laws that may also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for students (including student-employees) (§106.40(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide students with reasonable modifications as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to the education program or activity; where a student's pregnancy-related needs impact on-campus employment necessary to access education, §106.40(b)(3)(ii) provides the framework for addressing such needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consult with the student and apply a flexible, individualized approach; student-employees may be entitled to the same reasonable modifications in their employment context when needed to enable access to education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with other Federal laws — obligations not obviated
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in §106.57 relieves a recipient of separate obligations under other civil rights and employment laws, including Title VII as amended by the PDA, Section 504, the ADA, the PWFA, the PUMP Act, and provisions of the FLSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those laws may require reasonable accommodations or other protections; Title IX obligations are complementary and do not preempt State/local lactation or pregnancy laws that provide greater rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary leaves of absence for employees (§106.57(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not have another leave policy or the employee lacks sufficient leave or qualifying tenure, the recipient must treat pregnancy or related conditions as justification for an employee's voluntary leave of absence for a reasonable period of time and must reinstate the employee to the status held when the leave began or to a comparable position without negatively affecting any employment right or privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Reasonable period of time' is a fact-specific inquiry considering totality of circumstances, including medically necessary time as determined by the employee's healthcare provider; recipients with more generous leave policies must allow employees to use those policies instead; employees must not be forced to take leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical documentation requirements — equal treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may require medical documentation for pregnancy or related conditions only to the extent that such documentation is required of all employees with temporary medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to categorically prohibit documentation requests for employees (unlike the student provision), but reminds recipients that documentation may only be required if it is required for comparable temporary medical conditions of other employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation time and space — access requirement (§106.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must ensure that an employee can access a lactation space that is not a bathroom, is clean, shielded from view, free from intrusion, and may be used by an employee for expressing breast milk or breastfeeding as needed, and must provide reasonable break time to use it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language changed from 'ensure availability' to 'ensure that an employee can access' to emphasize functional accessibility; this mirrors student lactation protections in §106.40(b)(3)(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional standards for lactation spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a lactation space meets §106.57(e) is determined case-by-case; generally the space must be functional, appropriate, and safe for the employee's use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declined to mandate specific fixtures (chair, table, outlet, sink, refrigerator) or number/size to preserve recipient flexibility; recipients should consider Federal, State, or local laws that may set more specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility proximate to work — reasonable break time
rubrics_metrics.description: A lactation space must be accessible to the employee within the reasonable break time provided; if it is so far from the employee's workstation that they cannot use it, pump or breastfeed, and store milk in the time given, the space is not considered accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure the lactation space is usable within the allotted break time; the Department declines to set a specific proximity standard but requires practical accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared lactation spaces — accommodating multiple users
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple students or employees need simultaneous access to a lactation space, the recipient must develop a solution consistent with §106.57(e)(2) that meets the needs of the users—for example, signage, scheduling systems, or partitions/screens to allow multiple users simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department defers to recipients to determine the best arrangements consistent with the obligation to meet each user's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pumping and breastfeeding outside designated lactation spaces; presence of infants
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees retain the right to express breast milk or breastfeed outside designated lactation spaces if state or local laws allow; §106.57(e) permits using the lactation space for breastfeeding if the employee has access to their child while at work, but does not require recipients to allow infants throughout the workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of 'breastfeeding' in the regulation clarifies that employees may breastfeed in the lactation space; decisions about infants' presence elsewhere are fact-specific and may also be governed by state/local law; employees' choice of where to pump or breastfeed is subject to applicable laws and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and grievance procedures — non-exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may pursue claims regarding lactation or pregnancy-related rights under Title IX grievance procedures if they wish, but they are not required to exhaust Title IX remedies before pursuing other administrative or judicial remedies under other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations do not require recipients to add lactation information to employee handbooks as a standalone requirement; however, if comparable temporary medical condition policies are publicized, related notice obligations apply under §106.57(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-employment inquiries (§106.60) — asking applicants to self-identify sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory provisions permit recipients to make pre-employment inquiries and clarify that recipients may ask applicants to 'self-identify' their sex under certain conditions; technical edits were made for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reaffirmed its regulatory authority to require administrative actions that effectuate nondiscrimination in employment; commenters did not provide case law to the contrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Title IX (§106.10) — clarification of coverage of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations clarify the scope of Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination, aiming to ensure inclusive, safe, and supportive learning environments and to remedy discriminatory environments affecting groups such as LGBTQI+ and pregnant students; commenters sought additional definitions and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested examples (sex-based harassment, sexual violence, preventing participation consistent with gender identity) and debated whether 'sex' should be defined narrowly or broadly; the Department defended the broad framing as consistent with the statute and case law and noted discussions about regulatory necessity and executive-order considerations.
